words.gloss: to the people of the world

literal: Those who plough are the linchpin to the people of the world, supporting all those who, not performing that, rise.
translation: Those who plough are the linchpin of the world, for they support all others who, unable to plough, rise to pursue other callings.
modern: உழவு செய்பவர்கள் உலகத்தாருக்கு அச்சாணி போன்றவர்கள்; ஏனென்றால், உழவு செய்யாமல் மற்ற தொழில்களைச் செய்யப் புறப்படுபவர்கள் எல்லாரையும் தாங்கி நிற்பது அவர்களே.
explanation: This couplet highlights the central importance of agriculture to society by comparing farmers to a linchpin (ஆணி) of a chariot. Just as a small linchpin holds the entire wheel and chariot together, the farmers sustain the entire world. The phrase 'அஃது ஆற்றாது எழுவாரை' refers to those who do not or cannot perform the work of ploughing and instead rise to pursue other professions. By producing food, farmers bear the burden of supporting all these other professionals, making agriculture the foundational support of all human activity.
